_note: Every refinement in lib/schema.ts, with what it protects. The `fragment` on each row is a literal substring of the message that refinement emits, and the test suite asserts that every fragment is still present in the source and that the number of messages in the source equals the number of rows here. A guard added without a row, or a row left behind after a guard is removed, fails the tests. That is deliberate: a methodology page listing its own guarantees is worth nothing if the list can quietly stop being true.

categories.name: A published finding cannot go stale
categories.gloss: These encode a claim the site actually makes in prose. If the underlying numbers stop supporting the sentence, the build stops rather than the sentence going quietly wrong.

categories.name: Capacity must descend
categories.gloss: Built, then commissioned, then sold. Announced, then claimed, then handed over. A rung that rises means a row was misread, and that descent is the whole product.

categories.name: The parts must sum to the stated whole
categories.gloss: Wherever a filing prints both a total and its components, both are stored and the identity is asserted. This is what lets an exhibit say a figure is the issuer's own rather than our subtraction.

categories.name: Evidence cannot be overclaimed
categories.gloss: The primary tier is awarded by a check, not by an author. A row cannot call itself primary without naming a filed document.

categories.name: A comparison must measure the same thing
categories.gloss: A rate computed over a different set of topics, or a period compared against one that contains it, is not the same measurement however similar it looks.

categories.name: Impossible states are rejected
categories.gloss: Nobody can have more live capacity than announced, hand over more than is live, or have spent more on a project than it costs. These catch a mistyped row immediately.

categories.name: A claim must carry its evidence
categories.gloss: A graded forecast names what graded it. A refusal that points somewhere names where. Otherwise the register is an opinion with a schema around it.

rows.protects: The top three clients sum, to the second decimal, to the share of revenue the prospectus reports on contracts of at least seven years. The document never joins those two tables, and joined they say the durable contract base and the client concentration are the same three counterparties.
rows.fragment: The reconciliation that carries the finding no longer holds.

rows.protects: Clients one, two and three are Hyperscalers in every period. The concentration exhibit calls them that, and the filing is what says so.
rows.fragment: the filing states clients 1, 2 and 3 are Hyperscalers in every period

rows.protects: The same headline capacity figure is defined twice, on two different printed pages. If they ever land on one page the finding is gone, so the guard requires them to differ.
rows.fragment: the two capacity definitions must cite different printed pages

rows.protects: One government order is 69 per cent of the order book. An order larger than the book holding it would push that share past a hundred, which is arithmetic nonsense rather than a finding.
rows.fragment: cr order book it is measured against

rows.protects: The order book must be struck after the order was awarded, or the order is not inside it and the concentration exhibit is measuring nothing.
rows.fragment: does not postdate the award at

rows.protects: In every filed period, built capacity is at least commissioned capacity, which is at least what is sold.
rows.fragment: capacity rungs must descend, got built

rows.protects: The capacity rungs are stored widest first. The finding is that the widest one is an engineering maximum while being called built.
rows.fragment: capacity rungs must descend, widest first

rows.protects: Announced, then claimed operational, then actually handed over. That descent from 307 to 28 to 8 megawatts is the entire Anant Raj case.
rows.fragment: the capacity ladder must descend, got

rows.protects: The site rows must sum to the totals printed in the filing, within the rounding the filing itself introduces. A wider gap means a row was mistyped.
rows.fragment: sites sum to

rows.protects: The fresh issue and the offer for sale must add up to the total offer, so the exhibit showing how much never reaches the company is built on the issuer's own split.
rows.fragment: the fresh issue and the offer for sale must add up to the total offer

rows.protects: For each object, money already spent plus net proceeds plus borrowings equals the estimated cost. That identity is what lets the funding gap exhibit say the borrowings are the issuer's own figure rather than our subtraction.
rows.fragment: deployed plus net proceeds plus borrowings must equal the total estimated cost

rows.protects: A segment can never be larger than the group it sits inside, in any filed year.
rows.fragment: segment revenue exceeds group revenue in at least one year

rows.protects: Confirmed, partial, deflected and declined must account for every question pressed, so the refusal rate has a denominator a reader can check.
rows.fragment: the four response qualities must account for every question pressed

rows.protects: The per topic counts must add up to the stated denominator for the company.
rows.fragment: the family counts must add up to the stated denominator

rows.protects: The headline refusal count must match the topic breakdown beneath it.
rows.fragment: the refusal count must match the family breakdown

rows.protects: Every counted refusal must be listed individually, so a reader can read the numerator rather than being told it.
rows.fragment: every counted refusal must be listed, so the numerator can be read

rows.protects: A coverage row cannot claim the primary tier without naming a filed document. This is why only one operator in eight carries it.
rows.fragment: claims PRIMARY without naming a filed document

rows.protects: The capacity ladder on this page comes from a research note, and it may never claim the primary tier however often its figures are repeated. The annual report has since been read and sits in its own block with its own printed pages; this guard keeps the two apart, so the note cannot quietly inherit the report's authority.
rows.fragment: no Anant Raj figure is traced to a filing, so it cannot claim PRIMARY

rows.protects: The annual report prints one headline capacity number in its highlights and, elsewhere, the three pieces it is made of, only one of which is operational. Both are stored and the identity is asserted, which is what lets the exhibit say the composition is the company's own rather than our subtraction.
rows.fragment: the headline capacity figure must equal the parts the report says it is made of

rows.protects: No Netweb filing has been opened either, and the same guard applies.
rows.fragment: no Netweb figure is traced to a filing, so it cannot claim PRIMARY

rows.protects: Every company in the disclosure comparison must be measured over the identical set of topics. A rate computed over a different set is a different measurement wearing the same label.
rows.fragment: every company must be measured over the identical family set

rows.protects: Exactly one row in the issuer's chosen peer set is the issuer. Without it the peer exhibits cannot tell which bar to highlight.
rows.fragment: exactly one peer row must be marked self

rows.protects: The revenue mix exhibit draws a quarter against the nine months that contain it and says so out loud. Exactly one row of each, or that sentence describes rows which are not there.
rows.fragment: revenueMix must carry exactly one

rows.protects: Nobody can have more capacity live than announced. If that inverts, either a row was read wrong or an announcement has quietly been restated downwards.
rows.fragment: MW live against

rows.protects: What has been handed over sits inside what is live. Anant Raj is the whole reason this field exists.
rows.fragment: MW handed over exceeds

rows.protects: Money already spent on an object cannot exceed what the object is estimated to cost.
rows.fragment: money already spent cannot exceed the estimated cost of the object

rows.protects: A forward claim that has been graded must carry the evidence that graded it. An ungraded one stays open and says so.
rows.fragment: a graded claim must carry the evidence that graded it

rows.protects: A claim's horizon must fall after the date the claim was made, or it was never a forecast.
rows.fragment: horizon_end must fall after made_on

rows.protects: A refusal recorded as published elsewhere must name where. Refused on the call but published in a filing is ordinary investor relations; refused and published nowhere is a disclosure gap, and only the second is a finding.
rows.fragment: published_elsewhere requires naming where it was published

rows.protects: A single provider's published offer of processors must sit inside the number the scheme has installed nationally. The exhibit says one offer is more than half that national total, and past a hundred per cent the sentence stops being a comparison and starts being a sign that two different quantities have been put in the same ratio.
rows.fragment: offered more processors than the scheme has installed nationally

rows.protects: The government scheme's deployment ledger needs at least one provider reported ahead and at least one behind. That separation between announcement and delivery is the only reason the ledger is on the site, and without both sides the exhibit shows a list of names rather than a finding.
rows.fragment: the deployment ledger needs a provider on each side

rows.protects: Each of the eight operators in the peer benchmarking table carries one reading per fiscal year the table covers, present or explicitly absent. The source prints NA for operators that had not reported, and a short row rather than an explicit absence would shift every value after it into the wrong year.
rows.fragment: does not carry one reading per fiscal year the peer table covers

rows.protects: Every Indian operator in the table, not merely the issuer, earned a lower return on capital in the second year than the first. The sector page leads on that, so if one of them rises the page is claiming a decline its own primary source no longer shows.
rows.fragment: every domestic operator's return on capital fell across the first two years

rows.protects: A 2030 capacity forecast must exceed what is already operational. A projection below today's actual means a row was misread, or a publisher is forecasting a contraction and saying so somewhere this data does not record.
rows.fragment: MW already operational

rows.protects: Where a publisher gives a band rather than a point, its top must sit above its bottom. An inverted band would draw backwards.
rows.fragment: gives a band whose top is not above its bottom

rows.protects: A capacity forecast is a research house projection, not a figure read out of a filing, and cannot claim the primary tier however widely it is quoted.
rows.fragment: is a forecast and cannot claim PRIMARY

rows.protects: The exhibit claims the published forecasts disagree with each other by a factor of three. If one publisher held both the lowest and the highest number, that would be a single house's own band drawn as a disagreement, which is a different and much weaker claim.
rows.fragment: the lowest and highest forecasts come from one publisher

rows.protects: Three foreign firms have pledged more than the annual size of the entire Indian data centre market they are pledging into. That mismatch is the exhibit's headline. Below that line the pledges are an ordinary capital cycle and the exhibit has nothing left to say.
rows.fragment: no longer exceed the annual market they are pledged into

rows.protects: Three firms cannot have pledged more than every investor in the sector has committed in total. The exhibit draws the one inside the other, so past that point the two figures are counting different things and the drawing is meaningless rather than merely wrong.
rows.fragment: pledged more than the sector's whole recorded commitment

rows.protects: A corporate investment pledge is an announcement, not a figure read out of a filing, and cannot claim the primary tier however widely it is quoted. The same rule the capacity forecasts already carry.
rows.fragment: a pledge is an announcement and cannot claim PRIMARY

rows.protects: The capacity half of the pledge exhibit rests on one sentence: a single announced site is most of what the whole country currently operates. Only one of the three pledges named a capacity at all, so if either that figure or national live capacity moves, the sentence goes with it.
rows.fragment: the largest single announced site is under half of national live capacity

rows.protects: The government's estimate of data centre electricity demand must sit above what data centres already draw. A demand curve that does not rise has nowhere to go, and the page's claim that the grid rather than land or capital is the binding constraint rests on it rising steeply.
rows.fragment: does not rise above what data centres draw today

rows.protects: The capital requirement is drawn as a band from the low build cost to the high one. Inverted, it draws backwards and a reader sees a saving where the data says a range.
rows.fragment: the capex per megawatt band inverts

rows.protects: The stabilised colocation margin is quoted inside a published range for the same measure. A stabilising figure sitting outside its own range means two different measurements have been carried in as one, which is exactly the failure this project found in a capacity definition.
rows.fragment: the stabilising margin sits outside the published margin range

rows.protects: The page argues the grid is the binding constraint partly because electricity is the largest single thing a colocation operator buys. Under half of operating cost it is one line among several and the argument is weaker than the page states it.
rows.fragment: power is no longer the majority of operating cost

rows.protects: The consolidated income statement adds up to the profit before tax printed under it. Every line is typed from one printed page, and a mistyped expense would change the margin the page quotes while changing nothing a reader could see.
rows.fragment: does not reconcile to its own profit before tax

rows.protects: Cash generated from operations, less the income tax paid against it, equals the filed operating cash flow. All three are printed on the same statement and all three are stored, so the identity is asserted rather than assumed.
rows.fragment: less income tax must equal the filed operating cash flow

rows.protects: The movement in current borrowings is presented among the working capital adjustments inside operating activities, and the repayment of borrowings is presented again under finance activities on the next printed page. Both filed years do it. The cash conversion exhibit says the classification is the observation, so the document has to keep doing it: the guard fails if either side stops being an outflow or if the two stop being printed on different pages.
rows.fragment: must be an outflow in both the operating and the finance sections

rows.protects: Capital expenditure is the four lines the investing section prints. Against operating cash flow as filed it is more than covered; against operating cash flow with the borrowings line taken out it is comfortably covered. The exhibit's whole sentence is that one presentation choice moves the answer across one, so if a restatement ever lands both readings on the same side, the build stops instead of the sentence going quietly wrong.
rows.fragment: must change side when that line leaves operating activities

rows.protects: The data centre subsidiary is printed twice in the same annual report, once in the statement of subsidiaries and once in the consolidated entity table. Its net assets must agree across both, and against its own share capital plus reserves. That agreement is what lets the exhibit call the figure the report's own rather than a subtraction performed here.
rows.fragment: net assets do not agree across the two pages that print them

rows.protects: The same subsidiary's result for the year must agree across the two pages that print it. One is the statement of subsidiaries, the other the consolidated entity table.
rows.fragment: result does not agree across the two pages that print it

rows.protects: The data centre arm this company is priced on is about one per cent of the revenue the group actually reports. That is the deep dive's central claim, and above a tenth of group revenue the sentence is gone.
rows.fragment: the data centre arm is no longer a small share of group revenue

rows.protects: The data centre subsidiary made a loss in the year read. The page says the capacity everyone quotes sits in an entity that does not yet earn, so a profitable arm would be a different page and should fail the build rather than quietly change the meaning.
rows.fragment: the data centre arm no longer loses money

rows.protects: The group reports one segment and it is real estate development, which is why no data centre revenue, margin or asset line exists anywhere in the consolidated accounts. If the group ever reports the data centre separately, the central claim on that page changes and the exhibit has to be rebuilt rather than left standing.
rows.fragment: the group no longer reports a single segment

rows.protects: A risk row on this name may cite only a printed page the file already records, taken from the annual report block or from one of the source blocks on the audited statements. A page number appearing on a risk and nowhere else would mean a magnitude arrived without the source block that lets a reader check it. The register mixes rows resting on a research note with rows resting on the audited statements, so the rule is enforced per row rather than by banning pages outright.
rows.fragment: a risk row cites a printed page this file does not record

rows.protects: What is commissioned and live sits inside the three campus portfolio, which sits inside the capacity targeted by Fiscal 2030. This is the same descent every other operator on the site is held to, and an inversion means a campus was misread or a target has quietly been restated downwards.
rows.fragment: must descend from the target through the portfolio to what is live

rows.protects: The Noida campus carries a headline of 16 MW and a first phase of 500 kW, so the announced against delivered gap this site exists to draw appears inside a single site rather than only across an estate. If a restatement ever makes a stated first phase a material share of its campus, the sentence resting on it is gone and the build stops.
rows.fragment: a stated first phase is no longer a small fraction of the campus

rows.protects: The report is laid out as two page spreads, so one PDF page carries two printed pages and a printed page number can only run to about twice the PDF page count. A citation beyond that is a misread offset rather than a typo, and the offset is the single most likely thing to be wrong when a document is paginated this way.
rows.fragment: a cited printed page falls outside the document it is attributed to

rows.protects: A known limit marked closed must name what closed it, and an open one must not pretend to. Closing a limit is a claim like any other, and without this a limits list decays into a list of things that simply stopped being mentioned.
rows.fragment: a closed limit must name what closed it, and an open one must not

rows.protects: The document prints the return on capital formula inside its commissioned industry report and the answers in the business section, and never joins them. Rebuilt from the issuer's own key performance indicators, cash flow statement and balance sheet, every period that can be rebuilt lands on the published figure to the second decimal, and the exhibit says so. The earliest period is deliberately not covered, because an average needs a year the balance sheet does not carry, and that absence is itself the finding.
rows.fragment: the published return on capital no longer reconciles to the balance sheet

rows.protects: The filing prints cash generated from operations, the tax paid against it, and the net figure. All three are stored and the identity is asserted, so a mistyped row is caught rather than quietly changing the size of the funding gap the exhibit draws.
rows.fragment: cash generated from operations less tax paid must equal net cash from operations

rows.protects: Across every filed period taken together, spending on property, plant and equipment exceeds the cash operations produced. That is the claim the cash flow exhibit makes out loud: the estate was built with money the business did not generate. If it ever inverts the headline has stopped being true.
rows.fragment: no longer exceeds the

rows.protects: A printed page is what the primary tier means on this site, so the two have to agree. A secondary risk row that attaches a page is borrowing a filing's authority, and a row that cites a page while calling itself secondary understates what it actually rests on. Both directions are rejected.
rows.fragment: a risk citing a printed page must be primary, and one without a page cannot be

rows.protects: A risk row may only cite a printed page this file already cites elsewhere. The register is authored from what was read, so a page number appearing on a risk and nowhere else would mean a figure arrived without the source block that lets a reader check it.
rows.fragment: which this file does not cite anywhere else

rows.protects: The worst cell of the matrix, high severity against high likelihood, is the one a reader looks at first, and it cannot hold a row whose magnitude is not derived from data. The standard failure of a risk register is asserting a catastrophe with nothing behind it, and this refuses to render one.
rows.fragment: the worst cell of the matrix cannot hold an unmeasured risk

rows.protects: On the two pages where no filing has been opened, no risk row may cite a printed page or claim the primary tier. A risk sounds like a fact, so it is the easiest place for a page number to appear unchallenged, and one schema shared by both names means the rule is written once rather than twice.
rows.fragment: no risk row on a page with no filing may cite one

rows.protects: The same rule inside the measured register: a refusal that points somewhere must say where it points.
rows.fragment: a refusal that points somewhere must say where
